threads_text: OpenAI just released GPT-6.1 Terra, a mid tier model built to see your screen and click through apps for you, at half the API price of GPT-6.1 Sol. OpenAI says it finishes computer tasks more than 3 times faster than its bigger models. Would you let an AI drive your computer for a whole workday?
caption:
OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra on Monday, a fast model built for computer use, visual reasoning and clearer writing.
In the API it costs $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output, half the price of GPT-6.1 Sol.
It is rolling out in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users.

Would you hand your daily computer tasks to an AI agent?

paragraphs.text: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra on October 26, 2026. In its announcement on X, the company described the model as delivering fast and capable computer use at a lower price, saying it can understand what is on screen, take action across apps and write more naturally.

Terra sits in the middle of OpenAI's lineup. 9to5Mac lists the four model classes from lowest to highest price as Luna, Terra, Sol and Astra, and notes that when OpenAI released the GPT-6 versions of Sol and Luna in September, Terra was left on GPT-5.6. The new release moves it to GPT-6.1, about four weeks after GPT-6.1 Sol, according to iThinkDifferent.

The standard API price is $1 per million input tokens, $5 per million output tokens and $0.05 per million cached input tokens, half of GPT-6.1 Sol's $2 and $10, iThinkDifferent and Nerdschalk reported. OpenAI says the model costs 50 percent less than GPT-5.6 Terra, which it replaces. Batch and Flex processing cost half the standard rate, according to Nerdschalk.

The model is rolling out in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users. Developers can call it as gpt-6.1-terra through the Responses, Chat Completions and Batch interfaces, but not on the API free tier. Nerdschalk reported a context window of 1,050,000 tokens in the API and 500,000 tokens in Codex, with a knowledge cutoff of June 1, 2026.
What OpenAI claims it can do

According to results OpenAI reported and iThinkDifferent summarized, Terra completes computer use tasks more than three times faster than GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. On the Agents' Last Exam benchmark at maximum effort, OpenAI says it is more than three times as token efficient as Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 at one fourth the cost per token. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 at maximum effort it solved 50.3 percent of tasks, compared with 21.5 percent for GPT-5.6 Terra, although OpenAI still points to Sol and Astra for the hardest coding work.

OpenAI also reported fewer errors on an internal set of prompts designed to trigger mistakes. At low reasoning effort the error rate fell from 53.6 percent with GPT-5.6 Terra to 16.7 percent, and at maximum effort it fell by 18 percentage points to 4.3 percent, close to GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, 9to5Mac reported. The model reaches the Critical level for cybersecurity under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework and keeps protections built for GPT-6 Astra, iThinkDifferent said.

The release pushes computer use down into OpenAI's cheaper tier. Agents that read screens and click through software run long chains of steps, so price per token and speed matter more than peak capability, and that is exactly where Terra is positioned. All of the performance figures come from OpenAI's own testing, so independent results will matter.

Watch for independent benchmark results on computer use tasks and for whether Terra becomes the default model for agent work in ChatGPT Work and Codex, which would show how much everyday work OpenAI expects its cheaper models to handle.
